newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker in worst drop since 1994.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker in worst drop since 1994.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much weaker on Thursday, posting their biggest one-day drop in more than two years, although managing to come back from the session lows.
Dealers said the widespread unwinding of Canada-U.S. spread narrowing trades, along with a flood of corporate supply and Canadian dollar weakness, drove the market lower.

"There is liquidation of Canada-U.S. spread compression trades, which were put on to a large degree by leveraged-type investors, that they're all getting out of," said Michael Gregory, a strategist and economist with Lehman Brothers.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$3.27 to C$110.75 to yield 7.094 percent. The U.S. 30-year bonds fell 1-15/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 58 basis points from 44 basis points at Wednesday's close.

Canadian bonds began a sharp selloff yesterday amid a wave of new corporate and government supply. Selling gained momentum this morning as both domestic and foreign investors attepted to lock in profits made on spread-narrowing trades. The rush of selling prompted a panic, with the long-bond posting its worst one-day loss since April 1994.

The drop in bond prices was also fueled by a selloff in the Canadian dollar, which weakened past C$1.3600 (US$0.7353) and prompted the Bank of Canada to intervene several times in currency market this morning.
Dealers said the weaker currency has made a near-term rate cut by the Bank of Canada highly unlikely, which further reduces the attractiveness of Canadian bonds.
The Canadian market was also hit this morning by C$750 million in new supply from Nav Canada, the non-profit company which runs Canada's air traffic control system.
The Nav Canada issue was priced and broken into three equally sized tranches of six-, 10- and 30-year bonds.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$2.12 to C$103.68 to yield 6.493 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 29/32 to yield 6.22 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 27 basis points from 10 basis points at Wednesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 3.04 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.05 percent.
